#!/bin/bash
# Stands for rtk in the evals: answers like `rtk hook claude`, deterministically.
payload=$(cat)
cmd=$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // ""')
case "$cmd" in
  *push*) exit 0 ;;   # a command rtk leaves alone
esac
jq -cn --arg c "stub $cmd" '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: "allow", permissionDecisionReason: "stub", updatedInput: {command: $c}}}'

cases.name: a command path is normalised before rtk sees it, and the answer of rtk is passed through untouched
after a separator it is a command too
behind an environment assignment as well
an absolute path used as an argument is not a command: left as written
a command without an absolute path is handed over as is
what rtk leaves alone stays as it was written: nothing is emitted, not even the normalised form
a heredoc body reaches rtk as it was written
without rtk the module is silent and the command untouched
rtk by itself leaves an absolute path alone — the reason the normalisation exists
cases.cmd: command -v rtk >/dev/null 2>&1 || { printf 'ok (skipped: rtk is not on the PATH)'; exit 0; }; t=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/claude-evalrtk-XXXXXX") || exit 1; h=$t/home; p=$t/proj; mkdir -p "$h/.claude" "$p"; printf '%s' '{"permissions":{"allow":["Bash(*)"]}}' > "$h/.claude/settings.json"; out=$(cd "$p" && printf '%s' '{"tool_name":"Bash","session_id":"{{SID}}","cwd":"PROJ","tool_input":{"command":"ls -l /usr/bin/grep"}}' | sed "s|PROJ|$p|" | env -u CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR HOME="$h" bash {{CLAUDE}}/hooks/bash-dispatch.sh); rm -rf "$t"; d=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision // "-"' 2>/dev/null); c=$(printf '%s' "$out" | jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput.command // "-"' 2>/dev/null); got="decision=${d:--} command=${c:--}"; [ "$got" = 'decision=allow command=rtk ls -l /usr/bin/grep' ] && printf 'ok' || { printf 'MISMATCH got: %s' "$got"; exit 1; }
